'''Katalin Vesztergombi''' (born July 17, 1948){{r|hdc}} is a Hungarian mathematician known for her contributions to [[graph theory]] and [[discrete geometry]]. A student of [[Vera T. Sós]] and a co-author of [[Paul Erdős]], she is an emeritus associate professor at [[Eötvös Loránd University]]{{r|elte}}.

==Education==
As a high-school student in the 1960s, Vesztergombi became part of a special class for gifted mathematics students at [[Fazekas Mihály Gimnázium (Budapest)|Fazekas Mihály Gimnázium]] with her future collaborators [[László Lovász]], József Pelikán, and others.{{r|tgl}} She completed her Ph.D. in 1987 at [[Eötvös Loránd University]].{{r|hdc|mgp}} Her dissertation, ''Distribution of Distances in Finite Point Sets'', is connected to the [[Erdős distinct distances problem]] and was supervised by Vera Sós.{{r|mgp}}

==Contributions==
Vesztergombi's research contributions include works on [[permutation]]s,{{ran|PR}} [[graph coloring]] and [[graph product]]s,{{ran|XN}}
combinatorial [[discrepancy theory]],{{ran|SS}} distance problems in [[discrete geometry]],{{ran|LD}} [[geometric graph theory]],{{ran|GR}}
the [[Crossing number (graph theory)|rectilinear crossing number]] of the [[complete graph]],{{ran|CQ}} and [[graphon]]s.{{ran|D1}}{{ran|D2}}

With [[László Lovász]] and József Pelikán, she is the author of the textbook ''Discrete Mathematics: Elementary and Beyond''.{{r|dm}}{{ran|DM}}

==Personal==
Vesztergombi is married to [[László Lovász]], with whom she is also a frequent research collaborator.{{r|nol}}
